quote: Voluntary only; no price regulation; no federal agreement
correct_fact: In 2022 Vermont was operating under the Vermont All-Payer ACO Model agreement with CMS (performance years 2018-2022, extended; ended end of 2025). GMCB also already regulated hospital budgets (commercial rate increases) annually. 'No federal agreement' is false.
source_quote: VERIFIED_FACTS: 'Vermont All-Payer ACO Model: performance years from 2018; agreement with CMS ended at the end of 2025 (8 years).'
proposed_new_text: Voluntary ACO model under the All-Payer ACO Model agreement; hospital budget review but no reference-based price limits
notes: Local copy: sources/cms_vt_allpayer_aco_model_page.txt.

quote: Mandatory RBP (FY2027) and global budgets (FY2028) enacted; AHEAD signed Jan 2025 (withdrawn July 2026); \$195M RHT awarded
correct_fact: Act 68: RBP 'as soon as practicable but not later than hospital fiscal year 2027'; GMCB Feb 17, 2026 update: methodology set by rule in 2027, maximum rates effective HFY2028 (the chapter itself says 'prices from FY2028' at L5654/L5671). Global budgets: one or more non-CAH hospitals not later than HFY2028, 'to the extent that resources are available'. AHEAD/RHT parts correct.
source_quote: as soon as practicable but not later than hospital fiscal year 2027 ... Beginning not later than hospital fiscal year 2028, to the extent that resources are available ... one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals
proposed_new_text: Mandatory RBP (rule 2027; prices effective FY2028) and global budgets for at least one non-CAH hospital (FY2028) enacted; AHEAD signed Jan 2025 (withdrawn July 2026); \$195M RHT awarded

quote: All hospitals under Act 68 global budgets; Statewide Strategic Plan delivered Jan 2028
correct_fact: Act 68 requires global budgets for one or more non-CAH hospitals by HFY2028 and for all hospitals by HFY2030, both 'to the extent resources are available'. 'All hospitals' is not a 2028 target. Strategic Plan due Jan 15, 2028 is correct.
source_quote: VERIFIED_FACTS: 'one or more Vermont hospitals that are not critical access hospitals'; all hospitals by HFY2030, also 'to the extent resources are available'.
proposed_new_text: First non-CAH hospital(s) under Act 68 global budgets (all hospitals by FY2030); Statewide Strategic Plan delivered Jan 2028

quote: ON TRACK
correct_fact: After AHEAD withdrawal (July 2026), CMS's refusal of the Medicaid hospital global budget (payments stopped July 31, 2026) and the S.190 veto (June 16, 2026), 'ON TRACK' conflicts with the chapter's own partial-scenario discussion (Medicare alignment unresolved, L5687).
source_quote: VERIFIED_FACTS: 'CMS letter July 7, 2026 - not approved under Global Commitment STCs; payments stopped July 31, 2026'

correct_fact: (a) 76%/68% are 30-day follow-up after an ED VISIT for mental illness and for ALCOHOL USE (not SUD) among Blueprint PCMH-attributed patients, 2023 data, from the AHS Nov 2025 report (the same report's regional table gives 81% and 67%). correct_fact: RHRC engaging all 14 hospitals and contract concluding Oct 9, 2025: CONFIRMED (AHS Oct 2025 and Nov 2025 reports). source_quote: The 2025 reconciliation law, signed into law by President Trump on July 4, 2025

quote: Its healthcare provisions represent the largest single reduction in federal health-program spending in American history.
correct_fact: Searched KFF, CBO and CBPP for a 'largest ... in history' ranking; none found. KFF/CBO: the law reduces federal health spending by over $1 trillion over ten years.
source_quote: CBO has stated the law will reduce federal spending on health care by over $1 trillion (as reported by KFF)
proposed_new_text: CBO estimates that its healthcare provisions reduce federal health spending by more than \$1 trillion over ten years.
notes: Superlative rule: cannot source -> replace. The next sentence repeats CBO; the author may merge them.

quote: The Congressional Budget Office estimates \$911 billion in Medicaid spending reductions over ten years, producing an estimated 10 million additional uninsured Americans by 2034.
correct_fact: The 10 million is the whole law's effect (7.5M from Medicaid changes, 2.1M Marketplace, 0.4M other), not the Medicaid cut alone; 'producing' slightly over-attributes it to the Medicaid cuts.
source_quote: reduce federal Medicaid spending over a decade by an estimated $911 billion ... increase the number of uninsured people by 10 million
notes: Optional tweak: 'and estimates the law as a whole will leave 10 million more Americans uninsured in 2034'.

quote: The law imposes work and community-engagement requirements on Medicaid-expansion enrollees beginning January 1, 2027, requires eligibility redeterminations every six months instead of annually, caps state provider taxes, restricts state-directed payments, and phases out financing mechanisms that states have relied on for decades to fund their share of Medicaid.
correct_fact: Work requirements by January 1, 2027, but HHS may exempt a state acting in good faith until no later than December 31, 2028. Six-month redeterminations apply to expansion adults.
source_quote: by January 1, 2027 ... until no later than December 31, 2028
notes: Consistent with VERIFIED_FACTS (work requirements Jan 1, 2027).

quote: Congress included a \$50 billion Rural Health Transformation (RHT) Program in the same legislation, providing \$10 billion annually from FY2026 through FY2030 for state rural-health infrastructure investment. All fifty states received awards.
source_quote: All 50 states were approved, with first-year awards ranging from $147 million to $281 million ... announces awards, totaling $10 billion
notes: 'in explicit recognition of the damage' is characterization; not checked.

quote: The juxtaposition defines the policy moment: the largest healthcare-coverage contraction in American history, partially offset by a historic but time-limited and front-loaded capital investment in rural infrastructure.
correct_fact: No source found ranking the coverage loss as the largest in US history. 'Front-loaded' holds only relative to the cuts: KFF says the RHT dollars arrive before the back-loaded Medicaid cuts (the RHT itself is a flat $10B a year).

proposed_new_text: The juxtaposition defines the policy moment: a coverage contraction that CBO puts at 10 million people, partially offset by a time-limited capital investment in rural infrastructure that arrives before most of the cuts do.

correct_fact: KFF: the RHT could offset 'a little over a third (37%)' of the $137B rural Medicaid cuts; it partly offsets them, so 'does not offset' is too absolute.

quote: Before Medicaid cuts; 52% in non-expansion states (Chartis, 2026)

correct_fact: KFF/ACS 2024: Medicaid is the primary coverage of 19.5% of Vermont's TOTAL population (survey-based, primary-coverage hierarchy). State administrative enrollment is higher: 177,531 (June 2025, AHS) or 152,275 (Oct 2025, Medicaid.gov) = about 24-27% of the 644,663 population.
source_quote: Vermont 2024: Medicaid 0.19451 (121,400)
proposed_new_text: Medicaid is the primary coverage for roughly one in five Vermonters (Census survey data; state enrollment counts run closer to one in four) and is a significant revenue source for all 14 hospitals.

source_quote: the agency issued proposed regulations ... Comments on the rule are due by July 21.

quote: with the largest study to date (JAMA, 2026) finding real but modest savings --- about 16 fewer minutes of documentation per eight scheduled patient hours (§4.6.1).
correct_fact: Rotenstein et al., JAMA 2026 (doi 10.1001/jama.2026.2253): 8,581 clinicians at five academic systems; -16 min documentation per 8 scheduled patient hours. Matches Chapter 4 (L2683), verified in the 2026-10-12 Ch4 pass.

correct_fact: $1,030,000 allocated. Per the Ch4 pass, the scribe grants had not been awarded by April 2026 (NOFO due June 5, 2026).

quote: The next wave --- individual-level predictive population health, diagnostic AI as standard in high-volume imaging and pathology, AI-enabled triage that reduces unnecessary ED utilization --- is 18 to 36 months behind ambient documentation.

quote: Federal rules are moving in both directions --- the Section 1557 rule's decision-support provision now binds covered providers, while ASTP/ONC's HTI-5 proposal would roll back HTI-1's transparency requirements (§5.3) ---

notes: VERIFIED_FACTS.

quote: At full obesity-indication coverage for Medicaid and Medicare, GLP-1s would add hundreds of billions of dollars annually to program spending
correct_fact: KFF (BALANCE brief, 2026): covering GLP-1s for obesity in Medicare Part D is estimated at $25-35 billion over 10 years (CBO $35B) and Medicaid about $15 billion - tens of billions over a decade, not hundreds of billions a year.

quote: CMS's BALANCE Model (December 2025) is the federal attempt to thread this needle: negotiating lower GLP-1 prices to enable coverage expansion without fiscal catastrophe.
correct_fact: BALANCE was announced Dec 23, 2025. On April 21, 2026 CMS said it would not implement BALANCE in Medicare in 2027 (Part D indefinitely delayed); a Medicare GLP-1 Bridge runs July 1, 2026-Dec 31, 2027. The Medicaid component is rolling May 1, 2026-Jan 1, 2027.
source_quote: announced that it would not be moving forward with implementation of the BALANCE Model in Medicare in 2027 ... implementation will be on a rolling basis from May 1, 2026 through January 1, 2027
proposed_new_text: CMS's BALANCE Model (announced December 2025) is the federal attempt to thread this needle: negotiating lower GLP-1 prices to enable coverage expansion without fiscal catastrophe --- though CMS shelved its Medicare component in April 2026, leaving the Medicaid track and a temporary Medicare GLP-1 Bridge.
notes: Also affects L5650 'BALANCE GLP-1 access' (tailwind) - still valid for Medicaid.

quote: Vermont's DVHA must make a BALANCE participation decision in 2026 that balances near-term budget pressure against long-term population-health investment.
correct_fact: The state Medicaid RFA deadline was July 31, 2026, so the decision point has passed. Vermont's decision was not found (CMS BALANCE page, last modified 9/29/2026, lists no participating states).
source_quote: the deadline for the state Medicaid agency Request for Applications (RFA) is July 31, 2026
proposed_new_text: Vermont's DVHA faced a BALANCE participation decision in 2026 (applications were due July 31, 2026) that weighed near-term budget pressure against long-term population-health investment.
notes: Author should insert Vermont's actual decision if known; next sentence's 'should evaluate participation' then needs matching tense.

quote: The IRA drug-price negotiation --- semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) selected for 2025 negotiation, with negotiated prices effective in 2027 at roughly \$274 for a 30-day supply, down from over \$1,000 --- will meaningfully reduce the cost of coverage expansion for states and plans that participate in BALANCE.
correct_fact: CMS (Nov 2025): negotiated price $274 per 30-day supply effective Jan 2027, down from a 2024 list price of $959 (71% discount) - not 'over $1,000'. The IRA price is a Medicare price; it does not apply to Medicaid, and Medicare BALANCE was shelved in April 2026; the White House MFN deal ($245) is expected to supersede it.
source_quote: CMS has negotiated a 71% discount off the list price, or $274 for a 30-day supply ... [list price] $959
proposed_new_text: The IRA drug-price negotiation --- semaglutide (Ozempic, Wegovy, Rybelsus) selected for 2025 negotiation, with a Medicare negotiated price effective in 2027 of \$274 for a 30-day supply, down from a \$959 list price --- shows how far GLP-1 prices can fall, which strengthens the case for coverage.
notes: Also AMCP IPAY 2027 summary.

quote: VBC penetration is real --- roughly 58% of commercially insured Americans are in some value-based arrangement --- but it has not reached the tipping point at which fee-for-service becomes the minority mode of payment.
correct_fact: AHIP/HCP-LAN 2025 Measurement Effort (2024 data): 38.9% of private/commercial payments flowed through APMs in Categories 3-4 (down from 39.2%); 44.9% across all lines. No 58% figure; '58' is the number of health plans surveyed.
source_quote: just 38.9% of healthcare dollars made by private payers in 2024 ... 44.9% of healthcare payments flowed through APMs in Categories 3 and 4 ... 58 health plans
proposed_new_text: VBC penetration is real --- about 39% of commercial health care payments flowed through alternative payment models in 2024, and about 45% across all payers --- but it has not reached the tipping point at which fee-for-service becomes the minority mode of payment.
notes: The first sentence ('majority ... remains in fee-for-service') is CONFIRMED by the same data (55% in Categories 1-2). Also fix L5654 '~58% commercial'.

quote: The AHEAD Model --- now operating in five states (Maryland, Connecticut, Hawaii, Rhode Island, and New York), after Vermont's 2026 withdrawal --- is the most serious federal commitment to all-payer total-cost-of-care accountability since CMMI's founding.
correct_fact: Five states CONFIRMED (CMS AHEAD page: Cohort 1 Maryland; Cohort 2 Connecticut and Hawaii; Cohort 3 Rhode Island and New York). 'Most serious ... since CMMI's founding' is an unsourced superlative.
source_quote: Cohort 1: Maryland; Cohort 2: Connecticut and Hawaii; Cohort 3: Rhode Island and New York
proposed_new_text: The AHEAD Model --- now operating in five states (Maryland, Connecticut, Hawaii, Rhode Island, and New York), after Vermont's 2026 withdrawal --- is CMMI's current vehicle for all-payer total-cost-of-care accountability.
notes: Superlative rule.

quote: Changes implemented across all cohorts beginning January 2026 extended the model's end date to December 31, 2035, and added new requirements: each state must implement at least two policies promoting healthcare choice and competition, and adopt a Population Health Accountability Plan focused on preventive and chronic-disease care, with new transparency requirements around total-cost-of-care and primary care investment for Original Medicare beneficiaries specifically.
source_quote: AHEAD's end date for all cohorts is now December 31, 2035 ... states implementing at least two policies focused on promoting choice and competition in their health care markets ... new transparency requirements around TCOC and primary care investment targets
notes: Announced September 2, 2025.

quote: Maryland --- the model's longest-running and most-watched participant --- signed an agreement to continue its participation in November 2025, a signal that the federal commitment to this approach remains intact.
source_quote: On November 13, 2025, the state of Maryland signed an agreement to continue their participation in the model.

quote: Connecticut and Rhode Island both have existing cost-growth benchmark programs analogous in function to Vermont's GMCB, while New York's scale puts it closer to the "large, fragmented state" scenario discussed in the Introduction.
correct_fact: CT (Office of Health Strategy cost growth benchmark) and RI (OHIC cost trend target) have benchmark programs; the Introduction (L685-689) does discuss 'a large, diverse, politically fragmented state'. 'Analogous in function to the GMCB' is loose: neither program sets hospital budgets or prices as GMCB does.
source_quote: A large, fragmented state with a dozen competing systems does not escape this logic
notes: CT/RI benchmark existence is common knowledge; not re-fetched. The md shows straight quotes inside the box.

quote: Pennsylvania and several Midwestern states have active rural hospital transformation programs working on problems structurally similar to Vermont's Northeast Kingdom challenge, without AHEAD's federal framework.
correct_fact: The Pennsylvania Rural Health Model (CMMI rural hospital global budgets, launched 2019) has concluded; Pennsylvania is pivoting to its RHT plan (Health Affairs Forefront, Feb 2026). Since December 2025 every state has an RHT program, so 'rural hospital transformation programs' no longer distinguishes Pennsylvania or the Midwest.
source_quote: as the PARHM demonstration concludes, Pennsylvania is already pivoting to its Rural Health Transformation Plan (RHTP)
proposed_new_text: Pennsylvania's now-concluded Rural Health Model ran rural hospital global budgets on problems structurally similar to Vermont's Northeast Kingdom challenge, and all fifty states are now spending RHT funds on versions of the same rural problem without AHEAD's federal framework.
notes: Quote read from search excerpt.

quote: VT: Acts 167/68 form the most complete state reform mandate in the country.
correct_fact: Unsourced superlative; Maryland's statutory all-payer hospital rate setting is a competing candidate.
proposed_new_text: VT: Acts 167/68 form one of the most comprehensive state reform mandates in the country.
notes: Superlative rule.

quote: AHEAD operating in 5 states; VT mandatory RBP/global budgets as template; price-transparency momentum; BALANCE GLP-1 access.
correct_fact: AHEAD in 5 states CONFIRMED. BALANCE: Medicare component shelved April 21, 2026; only the Medicaid track (and a temporary Medicare GLP-1 Bridge) remains.
source_quote: announced that it would not be moving forward with implementation of the BALANCE Model in Medicare in 2027
proposed_new_text: AHEAD operating in 5 states; VT mandatory RBP/global budgets as template; price-transparency momentum; BALANCE GLP-1 access in Medicaid.

quote: VHCURES solid; VITL/HIE voluntary and incomplete; analytics vendor procurement underway; CIN in development.
correct_fact: AHS April 2026: analytics vendor contract under negotiation.
source_quote: the analytical support vendor contract is under negotiation

quote: VT CIN providing shared analytics and AI governance; RHT IT grants funding FHIR upgrades; ambient AI reducing burden nationally.
correct_fact: No RHT activity funds 'FHIR upgrades' (zero FHIR mentions in the RHT application and the March 2026 activity list). RHT funds EMR interoperability technical assistance, a voluntary shared EMR, e-Consult, telehealth and RPM.
source_quote: Grants may also be used to purchase tools and technical assistance to enable interoperability between electronic medical record (EMR) systems.
proposed_new_text: VT CIN providing shared analytics and AI governance; RHT grants funding EMR interoperability and a voluntary shared EMR; ambient AI reducing burden nationally.
notes: Same issue as finding on L5557.

quote: VT: RBP rule-making (2027; prices from FY2028); global budgets mandated (FY2028). National: VBC \~58% commercial; global budgets rare outside VT/MD.
correct_fact: (a) Commercial APM share is 38.9% (2024), not ~58%. (b) Vermont has no hospital global budgets operating: the Medicaid hospital global budget was halted (payments stopped July 31, 2026) and Act 68 global budgets start no earlier than HFY2028; Pennsylvania's Rural Health Model ran rural global budgets. (c) Act 68 global budgets are mandated 'to the extent that resources are available', for at least one non-CAH hospital in FY2028.
source_quote: just 38.9% of healthcare dollars made by private payers in 2024 [in Categories 3-4]; GCR 26-089: Medicaid HGB payments stopped July 31, 2026
proposed_new_text: VT: RBP rule-making (2027; prices from FY2028); global budgets mandated from FY2028 as resources allow; Medicaid hospital global budget halted July 2026. National: APMs \~39% of commercial payments; global budgets rare outside MD.
notes: The Introduction (L697) already says CMS halted the Medicaid hospital global budget.

quote: VT RBP producing documented savings; IRA GLP-1 negotiation (2027); Maryland AHEAD validating global budgets; ACO REACH maturing.
correct_fact: ACO REACH ends December 31, 2026; CMS's LEAD model replaces it from January 1, 2027.
source_quote: CMS has announced the Long-term Enhanced ACO Design (LEAD) Model as the successor to ACO REACH, which ends at the close of 2026 (search excerpt)
proposed_new_text: VT RBP producing documented savings; IRA GLP-1 negotiation (2027); Maryland AHEAD validating global budgets; LEAD replacing ACO REACH (2027).

quote: National: VBC \~70--75% commercial by 2030; global budgets stay limited absent mandatory policy.
correct_fact: A prediction anchored on the wrong 58% baseline. The commercial APM share was flat in 2023-2024 (39.2% -> 38.9%), which makes 70-75% by 2030 implausible.
source_quote: just 38.9% of healthcare dollars made by private payers in 2024 (down from 39.2% in 2023)
proposed_new_text: National: commercial APM share flat near 40%, rising slowly by 2030; global budgets stay limited absent mandatory policy.

quote: Blueprint among strongest PCMH infrastructure in the country; CCBHC expansion; CoCM Medicare billing enabling sustainable financing.
correct_fact: 'Among the strongest' has no ranking source; the same row's 2035 column then says 'strongest in country' - an escalation within one row.
notes: Hedged ('among') - acceptable; see the next finding for the unhedged version.

quote: VT: Blueprint PCMH infrastructure strongest in country; BH integration is the critical clinical variable.
correct_fact: Unsourced superlative, and it contradicts the hedged 'among strongest' in the tailwinds column of the same row.
proposed_new_text: VT: Blueprint PCMH infrastructure among the strongest in the country; BH integration is the critical clinical variable.
notes: Superlative rule.

quote: MHI sustainability uncertain without a durable funding source after the AHEAD withdrawal;
correct_fact: VERIFIED_FACTS: Medicare's primary-care money ended with OneCare; AHEAD withdrawn July 2026; RHT = stopgap.
source_quote: Medicare's primary-care $ ended with OneCare; RHT = stopgap.

quote: VT: hospital plans in development; AHS restructuring underway; PMO being established; CIN in development.
correct_fact: (a) All hospitals had submitted final transformation plans by April 2026 (AHS). (b) No AHS restructuring is underway: the Act 119 re-envisioning report (Feb 4, 2026) recommended keeping AHS unified ('feedback consistently favored better coordination over restructuring'), moving only clinical substance-use functions into DMH; Act 68 does not order AHS to reorganize.
source_quote: All hospitals have submitted final transformation plans. | VERIFIED_FACTS: Act 119 Feb 4, 2026 report: keep AHS unified
proposed_new_text: VT: hospital transformation plans submitted, implementation beginning; AHS kept unified after the Act 119 review; PMO being established; CIN in development.
notes: The same fix applies to L5658 headwinds '14 plans at varying stages' (see next).

quote: 14 plans at varying stages; analytics vendor not yet operational; AHS capacity must be built; RHT requires PM infrastructure VT is hiring.
correct_fact: Final transformation plans were submitted by all hospitals (April 2026); the plans are now at the implementation stage. The analytics vendor was not yet operational (contract under negotiation, April 2026) - CONFIRMED.
source_quote: All hospitals have submitted final transformation plans. ... the analytical support vendor contract is under negotiation
proposed_new_text: 14 final plans at varying stages of implementation; analytics vendor not yet operational; AHS capacity must be built; RHT requires PM infrastructure VT is hiring.

quote: \$195M RHT capital; all 14 hospitals engaged; GMCB capacity added under Act 68; joint AHS-GMCB analytics procurement; CIN shared services.
correct_fact: $195M, 14 hospitals engaged, and GMCB capacity (3 new positions for RBP) CONFIRMED. 'Joint AHS-GMCB analytics procurement': the RHT analytics vendor procurement is run by AHS (AHS April 2026 report: 'AHS staff are in the process of procuring vendors'); no joint GMCB procurement was found.
source_quote: AHS staff are in the process of procuring vendors to provide technical assistance and analytical support
proposed_new_text: \$195M RHT capital; all 14 hospitals engaged; GMCB capacity added under Act 68; AHS analytics procurement; CIN shared services.
